newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen hints solving Saudi border row may take time.
newsitem.headline: Yemen hints solving Saudi border row may take time.

text.p: Yemen's Prime Minister Faraj Said Bin Ghanem hinted in remarks published on Monday that resolving a protracted border row with Saudi Arabia could take time.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh said in early July a final settlement of the 61-year-old dispute was imminent.
Senior officials, including Yemen's and Saudi Arabia's interior ministers, have been shuttling between the two states in recent months to try to resolve the row.
"I worry about over-expectations created by the media," Bin Ghanem, an independent, said in an interview with the English-language weekly Yemen Times.
"There is no particular suggestion or project submitted for deliberation," he said. "There are proposals which keep on changing as negotiations continue."
Yemen and Saudi Arabia signed a memorandum of understanding in 1995 in an attempt to end the row. Since then they have exchanged high-level visits and held joint meetings.
The dispute has led to several minor clashes between the Arab world's richest oil power and one of its poorest countries.
"The Yemeni leadership, the political parties and public opinion in general regard this issue as a top priority," Bin Ghanem added.
